tldr: SkillVLA addresses combinatorial diversity in bimanual manipulation by discovering latent skill structures from demonstrations and flexibly reusing/recombining single-arm skills, achieving 51% success on unseen skill combinations where baselines fail near-zero.
contributions: Identified the skill entanglement issue in current VLAs (action entanglement via concatenated outputs and latent entanglement in action-expert architectures) and formally formulated the bimanual skill reuse problem
Proposed SkillVLA, a two-level reasoning architecture with a collaboration estimator that enables flexible skill reuse and adaptive per-arm vs. cooperative action generation

Validated SkillVLA on a real dual-arm robot across 20 manipulation tasks, two long-horizon multi-stage tasks, and a continual-learning study, demonstrating combinatorial generalization while maintaining cooperative performance
methods: SkillVLA uses a frozen high-level VLM (PaliGemma backbone from π0.5) that generates per-arm natural-language sub-prompts as skill descriptors, decoupling left and right arm selections. At the low level, separate fine-tuned streams (e.g., via LoRA) process visual input and per-arm prompts independently for single-arm skills. An adaptive cross-attention mechanism between action experts captures inter-arm dependence, gated by a cooperation estimator that predicts a scalar α ∈ [0,1]. The estimator is trained with a communication usefulness objective: L_coop = λ·L_on_BC − L_off_BC_sg · α_t, increasing α when cross-attention reduces behavioral cloning error. Additional regularization includes VLM-derived cooperation priors, sticky gating for temporal smoothness, and an optional discretization to α ∈ {0,1} with binary cross-entropy loss for stability.
results: On unseen skill-recomposition tasks, strong bimanual VLA baselines achieve near-zero success due to skill entanglement, while SkillVLA raises success to 51%. On three highly-cooperative tasks, SkillVLA matches baseline performance, confirming preserved inter-arm coordination. On two multi-stage long-horizon tasks interleaving collaborative and independent phases, SkillVLA correctly identifies cooperation levels and reduces execution time by 21% by recomposing skills to parallelize arms. In continual learning with limited demonstrations, SkillVLA effectively reuses existing behaviors for acquiring new skills, achieving significantly better performance.
limitations: The single-arm skill library is not explicitly available in practice; the model must discover and instantiate skill representations implicitly, which may limit discoverability for complex or ambiguous demonstrations
The cooperation estimator relies on behavioral cloning signals, which may not fully capture all nuanced coordination requirements in novel scenes
The paper notes that a continuous gate α_t can exhibit small persistent fluctuations that destabilize action generation, requiring optional discretization as a remedy
Evaluation is limited to 20 manipulation tasks and 2 long-horizon tasks on a single real dual-arm robot platform
